original_question: How can one classify diagrams in the flat hierarchy obtained by labeling flat crossings by elements of an ordinal and allowing a flat third Reidemeister move in which a line with two labels a slides across a crossing labeled b only when a is greater than b?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 3, “The Flat Hierarchy,” where the paper defines the hierarchy for any ordinal α and then asks for a classification of the resulting diagrams. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the target problem as the flat hierarchy, correctly includes labels on flat crossings coming from an ordinal, correctly states the special flat third Reidemeister condition that a strand meeting two crossings labeled a may slide across a crossing labeled b only when a>b, and correctly recognizes that the paper asks for a classification problem. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
missing_details: The paper poses the hierarchy for any ordinal α, so the quantifier should be explicit: the question is to classify the objects for each fixed ordinal α, or uniformly as α varies, rather than for an unspecified labeling set. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The objects being classified are flat virtual knot/link diagrams, not just arbitrary “diagrams”: these are diagrams with virtual crossings and flat crossings, where flat crossings are undecorated nodes of the 4-regular plane graph and virtual crossings are flat crossings marked with a small circle. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The relevant equivalence relation comes from the generalized flat Reidemeister moves for flat virtual diagrams, together with the detour move for virtual crossings; your draft mentions only the extra restriction on the flat third Reidemeister move. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

To be stand-alone, the rewrite should say that the classification is up to those moves, i.e. it is a classification of equivalence classes of labeled flat virtual knot/link diagrams in this hierarchy. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The paper does not ask for a specific algorithm, invariant, or normal form; it asks simply to classify the diagrams in this hierarchy, so the refined question should avoid adding broader goals. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

There are no ambient ring/field choices, variables, degree conditions, homogeneity assumptions, or nilpotency hypotheses in this problem; the missing structure is topological/combinatorial, namely the ordinal α, the labeled flat virtual diagrams, and the move system. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
refined_question: For each ordinal α, classify the equivalence classes of flat virtual knot and link diagrams in which every flat crossing is labeled by an element of α, where equivalence is generated by the generalized flat Reidemeister moves for flat virtual diagrams (including the usual detour move for virtual crossings) except that a flat third Reidemeister move is allowed only when the strand incident with two crossings both labeled a is slid across a crossing labeled b with a>b. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly aimed at Section 7, Problem 3 rather than a neighboring topic: the paper’s official formulation is the one-line open problem to classify the diagrams in the flat hierarchy, after defining that hierarchy using ordinal labels and the restricted flat third Reidemeister move. Section 2.1 supplies the hidden background needed to make that problem stand alone, namely what a flat virtual diagram is and what equivalence by generalized flat Reidemeister/detour moves means. The refined question therefore stays very close to the paper’s wording while making explicit the ambient objects and equivalence relation that the paper leaves implicit in the short problem statement. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
